claims.text: Rapid severe deformation followed by short-time, high-rate annealing will produce a hierarchical dual-phase microstructure.
The treated microstructure will contain an ultrafine-grained BCC matrix.
The treated microstructure will contain a finely dispersed network of coherent nanoprecipitates.
The hierarchical dual-phase architecture will activate nano-twinning or transformation-induced plasticity.
Supplemental plasticity mechanisms such as nano-twinning or transformation-induced plasticity will enable more uniform plastic flow and improved ductility.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will provide particle hardening that maintains high strength.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will help maintain impact-induced energy release.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically have predominantly BCC microstructures.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically combine high strength with limited ductility.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically deform non-uniformly under high-strain-rate or impact loading.
The proposed intervention is rapid severe deformation, such as high-rate forging or rolling, immediately followed by precisely tuned short-time, high-rate annealing.
The intervention should be effective under high-strain-rate impact and mechanical loading typical of energetic structural applications.
Relative to untreated material, the treatment will increase ductility and uniform elongation and reduce localized strain.
Relative to untreated material, the treatment will preserve comparable high strength.
Relative to untreated material, the treatment will preserve comparable impact-induced energy release.
Overly long annealing or insufficient deformation could cause precipitate coarsening or phase aggregation that compromises strength or energy release.
